rules.quote: Add alt text to all images.
rules.violation_condition: An image has no alt text.
rules.why: G-1: the requirement for alt text is independently checkable, unlike the heading grouping alt text, captions and titles.

rules.quote: Include captions for all images that are not decorative.
rules.violation_condition: A non-decorative image has no caption.
when: The image is not decorative.
rules.why: G-2: decorative status limits when the caption requirement applies.

rules.quote: Add titles to help users scan content.
rules.specification: The page does not specify which images need titles or how to decide whether a title is needed for scanning. This is not an explicit requirement to title every image.
rules.violation_condition: Image content lacks a title needed to help users scan it.
when: In the context of titles for images.
rules.why: G-1: image titles are a separate textual requirement from captions and alt text; the applicability remains underspecified.

rules.quote: All graphs, charts and maps should have a legend that tells people the meaning of lines, colours and symbols.
rules.violation_condition: A graph, chart or map lacks a legend explaining the meaning of its lines, colours and symbols.
when: The image is a graph, chart or map.
rules.why: G-1: explanatory legend text is independently checkable and is not combined with measurement labels.

covers.quote: Label the x- and y-axes, as well as legends, titles and captions as relevant.

rules.violation_condition: A measured quantity in a graph, chart or map is presented without its unit of measurement in the relevant labelling.
when: For measured quantities in graphs, charts and maps.
Units belong on axes, legends, titles and captions as relevant.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the list item identifies where the same missing-unit check applies, rather than creating a second labelling rule.

rules.quote: Use appropriate units (for example, millions of dollars for a company balance sheet but thousands of dollars for a household budget).
rules.specification: The examples establish that denomination should suit the context, but do not establish general thresholds for choosing units, thousands or millions.
rules.violation_condition: Measurement labels use a denomination inappropriate to the magnitude and context of the quantities displayed.
when: For units used in graphs, charts and maps.
rules.why: G-1: inappropriate unit choice is distinct from an omitted unit; E-4 prevents inventing numerical thresholds.

rules.quote: Use the appropriate number of decimal places on labels (for example, $1,000 – not $1,000.00 – for a scale of zero to $10,000).
rules.specification: The page rejects cents on a dollar scale from zero to $10,000, but gives no general rule for choosing decimal places on other scales.
rules.violation_condition: A numerical label has a number of decimal places inappropriate to the displayed scale.
when: For numerical labels in graphs, charts and maps.
rules.why: G-1: decimal precision is a separate check from unit choice; E-4 prevents extrapolating an unstated precision threshold.

covers.quote: Refer to informational images in the text
You don’t need to refer to decorative images and illustrations in the text unless they are part of the discussion.

rules.quote: Refer to complex images in the body of the text.
rules.specification: Use the body's scope of complex images. The later exception also makes a reference necessary when a decorative image or illustration forms part of the discussion.
rules.violation_condition: A complex informational image has no reference in the body text, or a decorative image or illustration is discussed without being referred to.
when: The image is complex and informational.
Decorative images and illustrations need no reference unless they are part of the discussion.
rules.why: G-2, G-3 and G-4: consolidate the heading, body requirement and decorative-image exception into one reference check.

rules.quote: Don’t repeat the whole caption of the image in the text. Instead, use a locator number to refer to it, for example ‘Figure 1’.
rules.violation_condition: A body-text reference repeats an image's whole caption instead of identifying it by a locator number.
when: When referring to an image in the body text.
rules.why: G-4: the replacement with a locator number explains the same caption-repetition check rather than creating a duplicate.

parts.quote: Figure 6 shows an example of good ergonomic posture.
The photograph of an ideal workstation set-up (see left) shows an example of good ergonomic posture.

rules.quote: Don’t refer to ‘the photograph on the left’.
rules.specification: Read the quoted wording as an example of inaccessible sensory identification, not as a prohibition limited to that exact phrase.
rules.violation_condition: An image reference relies on a sensory description such as its position on the left to identify the image.
when: When identifying an image in the text.
rules.why: G-1: sensory identification is distinct from repeating a caption; E-2 associates the nearby contrast pair with this check.

parts.quote: European Union expenditure more than quadrupled from 2016 to 2018 (Figure 7).
Figure 7 shows European Union expenditure increased from US$9 million in 2016 to about US$40 million in 2018.

rules.quote: Ensure your text comments on or interprets the image, rather than repeating the text or data in it.
rules.violation_condition: Text accompanying an image merely repeats its text or data without commenting on or interpreting it.
when: When discussing information displayed in an image.
rules.why: G-1 and E-2: this prose introduces a separate interpretation check despite appearing beneath an earlier example label.

rules.quote: Avoid referring to a page number in the text because page numbers can change during the publishing process.
rules.violation_condition: An image reference in print content identifies its location by page number.
when: For image references in print content.
rules.why: G-2: the Print considerations heading limits this textual reference check to print content.

covers.quote: List notes in the following order:
notes to superscript locators (such as a superscript ‘#’, ‘a’ or ‘1’)
source of data (use the appropriate form for author–date or documentary–note).

rules.quote: Follow the correct order for image notes
rules.violation_condition: Image notes put abbreviations, superscript-locator notes, a general note or the data source in an order other than the prescribed sequence.
when: When image notes contain any of these categories, their relative order is abbreviations, superscript-locator notes, general note, then source of data.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the heading and ordered list define one sequence check, not one rule for each note category.

rules.quote: Don’t include this information in the caption or in ordinary footnotes or endnotes.
rules.violation_condition: Information belonging in image notes is included in the image caption or in ordinary footnotes or endnotes.
when: For image-note information: abbreviations, superscript-locator notes, general notes and data sources.
rules.why: G-1: putting note information in the wrong textual component is distinct from ordering the notes.
